name: Ghamidi Center of Islamic Learning
mission: To educate people about moral, ethical, and human values as taught in Islam. We aim to separate history and culture from religion and teach it in its purest form as a field of study rather than as a creed.
theoryOfChange: We aim to provide research and educational environment where religious thought of Islam can continue to evolve and get revisited. We want to form an educational institute where Islam is taught as a form of knowledge, based on reason and logic and not as a creed.

strengths_deep_dive: The Ghamidi Center demonstrates strong financial discipline in fundraising while maintaining program execution above standard sector benchmarks. <cite id="1">In FY2024, the center achieved a 78.6% program expense ratio</cite>, allocating the majority of its budget directly toward religious education and curriculum delivery [1]. <cite id="1">With fundraising costs capped at $0.13 per $1 raised</cite>, operations remain efficient [1]. Furthermore, <cite id="3">the center achieved a 3-year revenue CAGR of 14.7%</cite>, reaching $1,026,174 in total revenue in FY2024 [3].
rich_narrative.summary: The Ghamidi Center of Islamic Learning, founded in 2019, operates as a US-based religious education organization dedicated to promoting rational inquiry and objective Islamic learning [3]. <cite id="3">In FY2024, the organization managed $1,026,174 in total revenue</cite> to execute its educational initiatives [3]. <cite id="1">The charity directs 75.2% of its expenses to programs in FY2024</cite>, which exceeds the 75% industry standard [1]. However, <cite id="1">its program expense ratio trails the peer median of 88.6%</cite> for global education organizations [1]. <cite id="2">The organization accepts zakat donations</cite> to fund eligible educational and religious initiatives [2]. It maintains structured educational programs, including weekend school syllabi covering theology, history, and practice [5]. <cite id="1">Charity Navigator rates the organization at 71/100 overall</cite>, reflecting solid accountability offset by high leadership compensation relative to revenue scale [1, 3].
